slides.title: Variadic Templates Overview
slides.prompt: Variadic templates accept an arbitrary number of arguments of any type using parameter packs (`typename... Args`). Introduced in C++11.

slides.title: Ellipsis Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator symbol used to declare a template parameter pack.

slides.title: sizeof... Operator Purpose
options: The number of elements/arguments contained inside the parameter pack
The total memory size in bytes of all pack elements combined
The byte size of the first argument only
A boolean indicating if the pack is empty
slides.correctAnswer: The number of elements/arguments contained inside the parameter pack

slides.title: Pack Expansion Operator Location
slides.prompt: To expand a parameter pack inside a function call expression, place the ellipsis ___ the pack name.

slides.title: Recursive Unpacking Pattern
slides.prompt: In pre-C++17 variadic templates, how were parameter packs processed element by element?
options: Using recursive function calls paired with a base-case overload function
slides.correctAnswer: Using recursive function calls paired with a base-case overload function

slides.title: Fold Expressions C++17
slides.prompt: C++17 introduced fold expressions to reduce parameter packs without recursion. Fill in the binary fold syntax to sum args.

slides.title: Fold Expression Types
slides.prompt: What is the difference between unary left fold '(... + args)' and binary left fold '(init + ... + args)'?
options: Binary left fold provides an explicit initial value when the parameter pack is empty
Unary left fold works only with integer types
Binary left fold evaluates arguments right-to-left
Unary fold generates slower machine code
slides.correctAnswer: Binary left fold provides an explicit initial value when the parameter pack is empty
